chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Salam in animals. He said, 'There is no harm in it.' I said, 'What do you think if one gives Salam in known teeth or a known item from the cattle, and gives it without the condition and above it, with their good pleasure?' He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.أَسْنَانٍ: Teeth (often used as a metonym for age or specific cattle)
key_terms.السَّلَمِ: Salam (a type of forward sale where payment is made in advance for goods to be delivered later)

ai.seo_question: Is Salam (forward sale) in animals permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of *Salam* (forward payment) in livestock, a key commercial instrument in Shia jurisprudence. He further clarifies that if the seller voluntarily provides a surplus or fulfills the obligation without strict adherence to formal conditions, out of goodwill (*bi-tibati anfusihim*), the transaction remains valid, highlighting the flexibility of Shia contract law in favor of the buyer.
